questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true?

1. If a body does not change its position as time passes it is at rest.

2. There is no meaning of rest or motion without the viewer.

Choose the correct code.
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Motion is a change of position.
 
• The motion of an object could be uniform or non-uniform depending on whether its velocity is constant or changing. 
 
• Newton's first law states that an object continues to be in a state of rest or of uniform motion along a straight line unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.
 
• The natural tendency of the object to resist a change in its state of rest or of uniform motion is called Inertia.
 
• Therefore, Newton's 1st law is also the called Law of Inertia.

Explanation:__

__
 
• Rest refers to an object being stationary relative to a particular frame of reference or another object.
 
 
• When the position of a body with respect to its surroundings does not change with the passage of time, it is said to be at rest. 
 
 
 
• Rest and motion are relative terms because they depend on the Viewer's frame of reference.
 
 
• If an observer is at rest in his or her own frame of reference but he may be moving in another observer's frame of reference. 
 
 

Thus, the correct answer is both 1 and 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Second law of motion states that the rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the applied unbalanced force in the direction of the force.
 
• Third law of motion states that to every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction and they act on two different bodies.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate definition of Newton's second law?

options.text: An object at rest remains at rest, and an object in motion remains in motion at constant speed and in a straight line unless acted on by an unbalanced force.
The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied
Whenever one object exerts a force on a second object, the second object exerts an equal and opposite force on the first.
The force needed to extend or compress a spring by some distance is proportional to that distance.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Newton's second law states that the force applied to an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration (F = ma).
 
• This law explains how the velocity of an object changes when it is subjected to an external force.
 
• The direction of the force is the same as the direction of the acceleration.
 
• This law is essential for understanding dynamics and the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion**

 
 
• This law is also known as the law of inertia.
 
• It states that an object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion continues in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force.
 
• This law highlights the concept of inertia, which is the resistance of any physical object to a change in its state of motion.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Third Law of Motion**
 
 
• This law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• It explains the nature of the forces between two interacting objects.
 
• If one object exerts a force on another object, the second object exerts a force of equal magnitude but in the opposite direction on the first object.
 
 
 
• **Hooke's Law**
 
 
• This law states that the force needed to extend or compress a spring by some distance is proportional to that distance.
 
• It is often formulated as F = kx, where F is the force applied to the spring, k is the spring constant, and x is the displacement of the spring from its equilibrium position.
 
• Hooke's law is applicable within the elastic limit of the material being deformed.

questions.question: The laws of motion describe how objects behave when they are in motion. Who among the following is credited with the formulation of these laws?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Isaac Newton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isaac Newton** formulated the **Three Laws of Motion**, which are fundamental principles describing the relationship between the motion of objects and the forces acting on them.
 
• These laws were first introduced in Newton's landmark work, **"Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica" (The Principia)**, published in **1687**.
 
• The laws of motion laid the groundwork for classical mechanics, which is a branch of physics that deals with the motion of macroscopic objects.
 
• Newton's First Law, also known as the **Law of Inertia**, states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• Newton's contributions to physics and mathematics earned him recognition as one of the most influential scientists in history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Second Law:** This law states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration (**F = ma**). It explains how the motion of an object changes when a force is applied.
 
• **Newton's Third Law:** It states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. This principle is fundamental in understanding interactions between objects.
 
• **Inertia:** A property of matter described in Newton's First Law, where an object resists changes in its state of motion unless influenced by an external force.
 
• **Classical Mechanics:** The branch of physics developed from Newton's laws, which deals with the motion of objects under forces and is used to analyze a wide range of physical phenomena.
 
• **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica:** Often referred to as "The Principia," this book not only introduced the laws of motion but also formulated the law of universal gravitation.

questions.question: A car is of mass 800 kg, is moving with a velocity of 144 km/h and the force exerted by the brakes to stop this car is 8 kN. Find the time taken to stop this car.
questions.solution:
__**Calculation:

Given:**__

Mass of the car (m) = 800 kg

Initial velocity of the car (u) = 144 km/h = 144 × (1000/3600) m/s = 40 m/s

Force exerted by the brakes (F) = 8 kN = 8 * 1000 N = 8000 N

We need to find the time taken to stop the car (t).

First, let's calculate the deceleration (a) using Newton's second law:

**F = m × a**

8000 = 800 × a

a = (8000)/( 800) 

**a = 10 m/s²**

Now, we can use the kinematic equation to find the time taken to stop the car:

**v = u + at**

Here, v is the final velocity, which is 0 m/s since the car stops. We know u = 40 m/s, a = -10 m/s² (negative because it's deceleration), and we need to solve for t.

0 = 40 m/s + (-10)× t

Rearranging the equation:

10 × t = 40

t = (40)/( 10) 

**t = 4 s

Therefore, the car takes 4 seconds to stop.**

questions.question: Consider a situation where a person is sitting in a car and is driving at a constant velocity in a straight line. If the car turns sharply to the left, the person will be pushed in which of the following directions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a car makes a sharp turn, the passengers inside experience a force due to inertia.
 
• This force is a result of the body's tendency to maintain its state of motion, as per Newton's First Law of Motion.
 
• If the car turns left, inertia causes the person to be pushed towards the right.
 
• This perceived force pushing the person to the right is often referred to as a "centrifugal force" in a non-inertial reference frame.
 
• The actual cause is the car moving left while the person's body tends to continue in a straight line.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion (Law of Inertia)**

 
 
• States that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• This law explains why passengers move in the opposite direction of the turn.
 
 
 
• **Centrifugal Force**
 
 
• It is a perceived force that acts outward on a body moving around a center, arising from the body's inertia.
 
• It is not a real force but rather a result of the inertia of the body in a rotating reference frame.
 
 
 
• **Inertial Reference Frame**
 
 
• A frame of reference in which Newton's laws of motion hold true.
 
• In such frames, objects not acted upon by forces move in straight lines at constant speeds.
 
 
 
• **Non-Inertial Reference Frame**
 
 
• A frame of reference that is accelerating or rotating.
 
• In these frames, fictitious forces, such as centrifugal force, are introduced to explain motion.

questions.question: A body of mass 10 kg is moving with a constant velocity of 10 m/s. When a constant force acts for 4 seconds on it, the body moves with a velocity of 2 m/s in the opposite direction. The acceleration produced in it is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-3 m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The initial velocity of the body is **10 m/s**, and the final velocity is **-2 m/s** (since it moves in the opposite direction).
 
• The acceleration can be calculated using the formula: **a = (v₂ - v₁) / t**, where v₂ is the final velocity, v₁ is the initial velocity, and t is the time.
 
• Substituting the values: a = (-2 - 10) / 4 = -12 / 4 = **-3 m/s²**.
 
• The negative sign indicates that the acceleration is in the opposite direction to the initial motion of the body.
 
• The correct answer, therefore, is **-3 m/s²**, which matches option 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:**

 
 
• States that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration (**F = m × a**).
 
• Acceleration is produced when a force acts on a mass, and its direction is the same as the force applied.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Acceleration:**
 
 
• Defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
 
• It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• Positive acceleration occurs when the velocity increases, while negative acceleration (deceleration) occurs when velocity decreases.
 
 
 
• **Opposite Direction Motion:**
 
 
• When a force causes a body to reverse its direction of motion, the velocity becomes negative relative to the initial direction.
 
• This reversal is characterized by a change in the sign of velocity and acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Force Application:**
 
 
• When a constant force is applied to a body for a specific duration, the change in velocity is uniform.
 
• Such scenarios are ideal for calculating acceleration using basic kinematics formulas.

questions.question: When an external force is not applied to the system, its total momentum ______________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Remains constant.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The total momentum of an isolated system of particles is conserved.**

 
 
• Its total momentum remains constant when an external force is not applied to the system.
 
• **The law of conservation of momentum** states that the sum of momentum of two objects before the collision is equal to the sum of momentum of two objects after the collision provided that there is no external force acting on it.
 
 
 
• **For a collision occurring between object 1 and object 2 **in an isolated system, the total momentum of the two objects before the collision is equal to the total momentum of the two objects after the collision.
 
 
• The momentum lost by **object 1 is equal to the momentum gained by object 2.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **If the net external force acting on a system is zero,** then its rate of change of momentum will also be zero.
 
• When an external force is applied to the system, and the body gains velocity, **the momentum increases gradually. **
 
• When an external force is applied to the system, and the body in motion started getting retarded,** the momentum decreases gradually. **

questions.question: Which of the following options is the same as Newton’s second law of motion?

options.text: Applied force on a body is inversely proportional to the acceleration of the body.
The rate of change of momentum of an object is independent of the applied unbalanced force.
An object at rest will remain at rest when external force is not applied.
If an object is in motion, applied force is directly proportional to the acceleration.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**If an object is in motion, applied force is directly proportional to the acceleration.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Newton's second law of motion states that the **force applied** to an object is directly proportional to the **rate of change of momentum**, and for a constant mass, it is directly proportional to the **acceleration** of the object. Mathematically, it is expressed as: **F = ma**, where **F** is the force, **m** is the mass, and **a** is the acceleration.
 
• It explains the relationship between the **force applied** on an object, its **mass**, and the resulting **acceleration**. This law is fundamental in understanding motion in physics.
 
• The second law is crucial for calculating forces in various applications such as **engineering, mechanics, and aerospace sciences**.
 
• This principle is applied in real-life scenarios like **vehicle acceleration**, the motion of projectiles, and the study of gravitational forces.
 
• It helps determine how much **force** is required to move or stop an object, which is important in designing machines and ensuring safety measures.

questions.question: What is the force acting on a body of mass 6 kg which changes its speed from 2 m/s to 3.5 m/s in 25 s?
questions.solution:
Given,

Mass (m) = 6 kg

Initial velocity (u) = 2 m/s

Final velocity (v) = 3.5 m/s

Time taken (t) = 25 s

To find the force (F) acting on the body.

We know,

F=m a {(From Newton's Second Law of Motion)}

Acceleration (a) is the rate of change in the velocity and = (v-u)/(t)

Therefore,

F=m((v-u)/(t))=(6(3.5-2))/(25)=(9)/(25)=0.36 N

questions.question: Which one of the following statements with regards to Newton's third law of motion is *not* correct?

options.text: Force never occurs singly in nature
When the earth pulls a stone downwards due to gravity, the stone exerts a force on the earth
There is a cause effect relation implied in the third law
There is no cause-effect relation implied in the third law

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**There is a cause-effect relation implied in the third law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's Third Law of Motion:-**

 
 
• The force exerted by an object A on an object B is equal and opposite to the force exerted on A by B.
 
• Newton's Third Law of Motion signifies a particular symmetry in nature that forces always occur in pairs, and one body cannot exert a force on another without experiencing a force itself.
 
 
 
• According to **Newton's third law**, the stone exerts an equal and opposite force on the earth.
 
• Since the earth is very massive and the effect of a small force on its motion is negligible.
 
• Force is the mutual interaction between two bodies.
 
• Forces between two bodies are always equal and opposite which is given by Newton's third law of motion.
 
• **There is no cause-effect relation implied in the third law. **
 
• The force on A by B and the force on B by A act at the same instant.
 
• By the same reasoning, any one of them may be action and another reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton’s first law **states that, if a body is at rest or moving at a constant speed in a straight line, it will remain at rest or keep moving in a straight line at constant speed unless it is acted upon by a force.
 
• This postulate is known as the** law of inertia**.
 
• **Newton’s second law** is a quantitative description of the changes that a force can produce on the motion of a body.
 
• It states that the** time rate of change of the momentum of a body is equal in both magnitude and direction to the force imposed on it**.
 
• The **momentum** of a body is equal to the** product of its mass and its velocity.**

questions.question: An astronaut accidentally gets separated out of his small spaceship accelerating in inter stellar space at a constant rate of 100 m s-2. The acceleration of the astronaut the instant after he is outside the spaceship is Zero. This is in accordance with _________.

options.text: Law of conservation of linear momentum

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton's first law of motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Newton's first law of motion, also known as the law of inertia, states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• The astronaut, once separated from the spaceship, will continue to move at the same velocity it had at the moment of separation, due to the absence of any external force acting on him.
 
• The instant after separation, the astronaut experiences zero acceleration because no forces are acting on him in the vacuum of interstellar space.
 
• This principle is directly derived from Newton's first law, which underscores the concept that in the absence of a net external force, the acceleration of an object is zero.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion**

 
 
• Newton's first law (Law of Inertia): An object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• Newton's second law: The force acting on an object is equal to the mass of that object times its acceleration (F=ma).
 
• Newton's third law: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
 
 
• **Inertia**
 
 
• Inertia is the resistance of any physical object to a change in its state of motion or rest.
 
• It is directly related to the mass of the object; higher mass means higher inertia.
 
 
 
• **Interstellar Space**
 
 
• Interstellar space is the physical space within a galaxy beyond the influence of any single star system.
 
• It is largely a vacuum with very low density of particles, making it an ideal environment to observe the effects of Newton's first law.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration**
 
 
• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity of an object with respect to time.
 
• In the absence of an external force, an object will not experience acceleration, as per Newton's first law.

questions.question: Which of the following is a consequence of Newton's Second Law of Motion?

options.text: By applying the same force, a car gains more acceleration than a truck shall gain.
A gun recoils after shooting a bullet.
When we run on a carpet, it moves backwards.
When we push someone, we tend to move backwards.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Newton's Second Law of Motion states that the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass **(F = ma)**.
 
• This implies that for the same force applied, the object with lesser mass will experience greater acceleration.
 
• In the given options, a car typically has less mass compared to a truck; hence, for the same force, the car will accelerate more than the truck.
 
• Newton's Second Law is fundamental in understanding the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration.
 
• This law is crucial in fields such as engineering, physics, and various applications involving motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion**

 
 
• Also known as the law of inertia, it states that an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion unless acted upon by a net external force.
 
• This law explains the resistance of objects to change their state of motion.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Third Law of Motion**
 
 
• It states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• This law is observable in scenarios such as the recoil of a gun when a bullet is fired.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Newton's Laws**
 
 
• These laws form the basis for classical mechanics and are used extensively in designing vehicles, machinery, and understanding natural phenomena.
 
• They are also crucial in calculating forces in static and dynamic systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct expression for the calculation of centrifugal force (F) experienced by an object during its curvilinear motion. Where, w = Weight of revolving object, v = velocity at radius 'r' on body, g = acceleration due to gravity, r = perpendicular distance from axis of rotation to centre of gravity of revolving object.
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

Centripetal force:

__
 
• Centripetal force is the force acting on an object in curvilinear motion directed towards the axis of rotation or center of curvature.
 
• The centripetal force is always directed perpendicular to the direction of the object’s displacement.
 
• Using Newton’s second law of motion, it is found that the centripetal force of an object moving in a circular path always acts towards the center of the circle.

The formula for centripetal force,

 F=ma꜀

a꜀=frac{v²}{r} 

F=ma꜀=frac{mv²}{r} 

w = mg

m = w/g

F=frac{{w}v²}{gr} 

Where,

 
• F is the Centripetal force.
 
• ac is the Centripetal acceleration.
 
• m is the mass of the object.
 
• v is the speed or velocity of the object.
 
• r is the radius.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Rectilinear

 
• The linear motion also called rectilinear motion, is one-dimensional motion along a straight line, and can therefore be described mathematically using only one spatial dimension.
 
• Linear motion can be of two types: uniform linear motion, with constant velocity; and non-uniform linear motion, with variable velocity.

 Curvilinear

 
• The motion of an object moving in a curved path is called curvilinear motion.
 
• Example: A stone thrown into the air at an angle.
 
• The curvilinear motion describes the motion of a moving particle that conforms to a known or fixed curve.

questions.question: A body of mass 10 kg is acted upon by two perpendicular forces 6 N and 8 N. What will be the magnitude of acceleration of body
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a = 1 ms⁻²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Two perpendicular forces, 6 N and 8 N, act on the body. The resultant force can be calculated using the **Pythagorean theorem** as F = √(6² + 8²) = 10 N.
 
• The mass of the body is given as **10 kg**. According to Newton's second law, acceleration (a) is calculated as a = F/m.
 
• Substituting the values: a = 10 N / 10 kg = **1 ms⁻²**.
 
• Since the forces are perpendicular, the resultant acceleration is along the direction of the resultant force.
 
• The correct magnitude of acceleration is **1 ms⁻²**, corresponding to option 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:**

 
 
• It states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration (F = ma).
 
• This law explains how the velocity of an object changes when it is subjected to an external force.
 
 
 
• **Resultant Force Calculation:**
 
 
• When two forces act perpendicular to each other, their resultant is calculated using the Pythagorean theorem: F = √(F₁² + F₂²).
 
• For forces 6 N and 8 N, the resultant is 10 N.
 
 
 
• **Unit of Acceleration:**
 
 
• Acceleration is measured in meters per second squared (ms⁻²).
 
• It represents the rate of change of velocity per unit of time.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Newton's Second Law:**
 
 
• It is widely used to calculate motion parameters in mechanics, engineering, and aerospace dynamics.
 
• Understanding this law is fundamental to solving problems involving forces and motion.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Newton's second law of motion?

options.text: An object thrown in outer space
Resting against a wall or tree

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Car crash.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **During a car crash,** there exists a force between the obstacle and the car, which is known as the impact force.

 
 
• The magnitude of the impact force depends on the mass of the objects involved in the collision and the speed with which the objects move.
 
• **This means that the greater the mass of the objects involved in the collision, the more will be the intensity of the impact force.**
 
• Similarly, the more the acceleration with which the car moves, the greater will be the magnitude of the impact force.
 
• **Force, F = ma where, m=mass, a= acceleration.**
 
• This is an **example of Newton's second law of motion.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **If an object is thrown into outer space,** it tends to move in a direction to infinity.

 
 
• This is because outer space lacks the environment, air, and the force of gravity.
 
• Hence, the object does not receive any resistance to the motion, therefore, it continues to exhibit motion until it hits a celestial body, strikes a meteorite, or enters the gravitational field of a planet,** thereby demonstrating the first law of motion in real life.**
 
 
 
• **When the branch of a tree is vigorously shaken** with the help of an external force, it comes to motion, however, the leaves attached to the branch do not comprehend the motion and tend to maintain their state of rest.
 
 
• The motion of the branch of the tree and the inertia of rest exhibited by the leaves cause the shedding of leaves. 
 
• **It's another example of Newton's first law of motion.**
 
 
 
• **When we rest against a tree or a wall,** we get reaction force from the tree or the wall in order to support us.
 
 
• We can understand this example by imagining if someone is to rest on us, then we have to apply some force to support the other person.
 
• **This example of Newton's third law is also an example of balanced forces. **

questions.question: What is the type of force applied while pushing a car?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muscular Force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The force applied while pushing a car is **muscular force**, which is generated by the muscles in the body.
 
• When a person pushes a car, their muscles exert force on the car in the direction they want to move it. This force is transmitted through the body to the car.
 
• Unlike other forces, such as friction or gravitational force, **muscular force** is a voluntary force, controlled by the action of muscles and bones.
 
• The **magnitude of muscular force** depends on factors such as the individual's strength, endurance, and how effectively they can exert force on the object being pushed.
 
• In everyday scenarios, muscular force is essential for moving objects, lifting, and other physical activities requiring human effort.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frictional Force** – This force is present between two surfaces in contact and resists the relative motion of the objects. In the case of pushing a car, friction also plays a role in preventing or limiting the car's movement based on the surface.
 
• **Gravitational Force** – This is the force exerted by the Earth on the car, pulling it downwards. However, it does not directly relate to the action of pushing the car unless it contributes to the car's weight.
 
• **Applied Force** – This is a general term for any force applied to an object, but it does not specifically refer to the action of using human muscles to push the car.
 
• **Tension Force** – This force occurs when an object is being pulled, such as a rope or string, and does not apply directly to the act of pushing a car.

questions.question: Two objects of masses of 100 gm and 200 gm are moving along the same line and direction with velocities of 2 m/s and 1 m/s, respectively. They collide, and after the collision, the first object moves at a velocity of 1.67 m/s. Determine the velocity of the second object.

**Explanation:**

Given **m₁=100g=0.1kg, m₂=200g=0.2kg**

**u₁ = 2 m/s, u₂ =1 m/s, v₁= 1.67 m/s, v₂=?**

By the law of conservation of momentum,

**m₁u₁+ m₂u₂= m₁v₁+m₂v₂**

Substituting all the respective values in the above equation gives

**0.1 × 2 + 0.2 × 1 = 0.1 × 1.67 + 0.2 v 2 **

**Therefore v₂ = 1.165 m/s**

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Newton's third law of motion?

options.text: Applying brake in a moving bus

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The recoil of a gun**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The recoil in a gun** is caused due to the forward momentum of the bullet.

 
 
• The force with which the bullet is fired is balanced by the recoil of the gun.
 
• The gunman gets a jerk on firing a bullet from his gun.
 
• This is because when a bullet is fired from a gun, the force sending the bullet forward is equal to the force sending the gun backwards but due to the high mass of the gun, it moves only a little distance backwards giving a jerk to the gunman.
 
• So,** the recoil follows Newton's third law of motion**. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

__
 
• The** launching of rockets **is based on the **principle of the law of conservation of momentum,** while the **recoil of the gun** is an example of **Newton's third law of motion i.e. momentum.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A marathon runner is not able to stop himself right after crossing the finish line**.

 
 
• He/she tends to take time and cover a few meters of distance running beyond the finish line.
 
• This is because the **inertia of motion or Newton's first law of motion** resists a sudden termination of motion and compels the body to maintain its state of motion.
 
 
 
• **For a rocket to leave the earth's orbit** and enter outer space, a force called thrust is required.
 
 
• As per the **second law of motion given by Sir Issac Newton,** the force is proportional to the acceleration, therefore, to launch a rocket, the magnitude of thrust is increased, which in turn increases the acceleration.
 
• The speed achieved by the rocket finally helps it to escape the earth's gravitational field and enter space.
 
 
 
• In simple terms,** Newton's second law of motion states that if force is applied to any object that has mass, it will result in the production of an equivalent amount of acceleration in the object.**
 
 
• For instance, when we turn on the ignition system of the car, the engine of the car produces a sufficient force that enables the car to move with **proportionate acceleration. **

questions.question: A sports shooter fires a bullet of mass 30 g horizontally from his pistol weighing 1 kg with a velocity of 100 m/s. What is the recoil velocity of the pistol?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-3 m/s**__**.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's third law **of motion states that when one object exerts a force on another object, the second object instantaneously exerts a force back on the first due to which **momentum gets conserved.**
 
• 
 These two forces are always **equal **in magnitude but opposite in direction.
 
 
• When a gun is fired, 
 
 
• it exerts a forward force on the bullet. 
 
• The bullet exerts an equal and opposite force on the gun. 
 
• This results in the recoil of the gun.
 
 

​**CALCULATION:**__

__
 
• Given, 

 
 
• mass of the bullet (m₁) = 30 g = 0.03 kg, mass of the pistol (m₂) = 1 kg
 
• The initial velocity of bullet (u₁) and pistol (u₂) = 0, the final velocity of bullet *v₁* = 100 m/s, Recoil velocity(*v*) = ?
 
 
 
• Total momenta of the pistol and bullet before the fire, when the gun is at rest, is given by 
 
 
• ​​p₁= mass (m₁ + m₂) x velocity (u₂)
 
 

 = (1 + 0.03) kg × 0 m/s= 0 m/s

 
• Total momenta (p) of the pistol and bullet after it is fired is given by

 
 
• ​​​p₂= mass (m₂) x velocity (v) + mass (m₁) x velocity (v₁)
 
 

 = 1 kg × *v *m/s + 0.03 kg × ( 100 m/s)

 = (3 + v) kg m/s

 

 
• According to the law of conservation of momentum, 

 
 
• **Total momenta after the fire = Total momenta before the fire **
 
• That is, p₂ = p1
 
 

 3 + *v *= 0

 *v *= - 3 m/s

 
• Hence, the recoil velocity of the pistol is -3 m/s.
 
• The **negative sign indicates that the direction** in which the pistol would recoil is opposite to that of the bullet, that is, right to left.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **The first law of motion**: An object continues to be in a state of rest or of uniform motion along a straight line unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.
 
• 
 **The second law of motion**: The rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the applied unbalanced force in the direction of the force.
 
 
• 
 
 **Third law of motion**: To every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction and they act on two different bodies.

questions.question: The rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the applied unbalanced force in the direction of force. This is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**second law of motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• 
 
**second law of motion:**

 
 
• Newton's second law of motion states that the rate of change of momentum of an object is directly proportional to the applied unbalanced force and takes place in the direction of the force.
 
• Mathematically, it is expressed as F = ma, where F is the force, m is the mass, and a is the acceleration.
 
• This law explains how forces cause changes in motion.
 
• It is the fundamental law that relates force to acceleration.
 
• The change of momentum is equal to the impulse of the force.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
**law of inertia:**

 
 
• The law of inertia is also known as Newton's first law of motion.
 
• It states that an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion with a constant velocity, unless acted upon by an unbalanced force. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• It describes the tendency of objects to resist changes in their state of motion.
 
• It is the law that defines inertia.
 
• Inertia is the resistance of any physical object to any change in its velocity.
 
 
 
• 
 
**first law of motion:**

 
 
• Newton's first law of motion is essentially the law of inertia.
 
• It defines inertia and explains how objects behave in the absence of external forces.
 
• It sets the foundation for understanding how forces affect motion.
 
• It is the law of unforced motion.
 
• An object will continue to do whatever it is doing, until a force acts upon it.
 
 
 
• 
 
**third law of motion:**

 
 
• Newton's third law of motion states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• This means that when one object exerts a force on another object, the second object exerts an equal and opposite force on the first object. 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
• This law explains how forces occur in pairs.
 
• It is the law of action and reaction.
 
• Forces always come in pairs.

questions.question: Unless acted upon by an external force, an object at rest remains at rest, or if in motion, it continues to move in a straight line with constant speed. Which law states this?

__
 
• Unless acted upon by an external force, an object at rest remains at rest, or if in motion, it continues to move in a straight line with constant speed. 
 
• This is the **law of inertia**__, also known as Newton's first law of motion.
 
• **Law of force **is the **second law of motion of Newton**, which states that the time rate of change of a body's momentum is equal in both direction and magnitude of the force imposed on it.
 
• **Third law of motion**- Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
